subject: Ledger timestamp mismatch causing withheld payout — BrightApps evidence
messages:
From: BrightApps Billing <billing@brightapps.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Missing payout for MAY usage — invoice shows duplicate lines

Hi Stephanie,

We noticed our May marketplace payout was withheld and the invoice (attached) shows what appears to be duplicate metered lines for two SKUs that map to the same tenant. BrightApps' finance team pulled our ledger and we see two different timestamps for the same usage records (one in UTC, one in PT), which looks like a metering/aggregation mismatch on Redwood's side. Can you confirm what caused the duplicate rows and whether you can release the withheld payout?

Attached: brightapps_invoice_MAY2027.pdf, sample_ledger_rows.csv

We need the payment cleared by next week for our payroll cutoff. If you need additional evidence, we can export our internal usage traces.

Thanks,

- If it's our aggregation, can we issue either a credit memo or expedite the payout? BrightApps requests payout by 31 May.

Stef

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: BrightApps Billing <billing@brightapps.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Missing payout for MAY usage — invoice shows duplicate lines

On Thu, May 20, 2027 at 09:45 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> David/Monica — forwarding BrightApps' note.

I pulled the marketplace ingestion logs and raw CSV dump from our meter-ingest bucket. Initial findings: there are two metering events for the same usage_id in our raw file with timestamps that differ by exactly 7 hours (2027-05-12T03:24:00Z vs 2027-05-11T20:24:00-07:00). The marketplace (AWS) provides timestamps in UTC; our pipeline should normalize to UTC, but an edge-case in the older ETL job for legacy SKUs left timestamps in local timezone. Sequence: ingestion -> prefix cache -> dedupe window (10s). The dedupe window used ingestion_time rather than reported_timestamp for these SKUs, so entries slipped through as unique.

Action items I propose:
1) Export the full raw metering dump for BRIGHT-67890 (attached aws_metering_raw_202705.csv) and run a dedupe by canonical usage_id + normalized timestamp.
2) If dedupe drops rows that were billed twice, prepare a credit memo for the duplicate amount and mark payout to be released.
3) Raise a runtime fix: update the ETL to use reported_timestamp normalization for legacy SKUs and add a regression test.

I can run the reconciliation this afternoon and attach a delta. Monica — can you own credit memo and payout release path once I confirm the delta?

- David
Senior Finance Engineer
Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightApps Billing <billing@brightapps.com>, aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Missing payout for MAY usage — invoice shows duplicate lines

Thanks David — I ran the reconciliation and attached the delta file (brightapps_delta_202705.csv) and a proposed credit memo draft. Summary:
- Duplicate billed amount: $12,430.00 (two metered lines for the same usage_id).
- Root cause: ingestion job ingest-etl-v2 did not normalize the legacy SKU timestamps; dedupe used ingestion_time.

Proposed resolution:
- Issue credit memo CM-2027-093 to BrightApps for $12,430.00 (covers duplicates).
- Release withheld payout after credit memo is applied; expedite via internal billing ops (payment run ID: PAYRUN-202705-EX).
- Deploy ETL patch to master and schedule hotfix rollout to avoid June duplication.

Monica attaching: brightapps_delta_202705.csv, draft_credit_memo_CM-2027-093.pdf, redwood_etl_patch_diff.txt

BrightApps — can you confirm acceptance of credit memo or do you prefer immediate gross payout + separate invoice for reversal? If they accept CM we'll apply to May statement and release the net payment.

Monica Patel
Billing Lead, Marketplace Finance
monica.patel@redwood.ai
